scope: THE SNAPSHOT HAS TWO CURSORS: the bit reader and a separate BYTE reader - and the entity count comes from the BYTE one

the_count_reader_0x66ed70.0x66ED7C: cmp ecx,eax ; jge 0x66EDB5  -> overrun: set the error flag at [edx] and return -1
the_count_reader_0x66ed70.0x66ED80: cmp ecx,esi ; jl 0x66ED97  -> below the window: read from the [edx+8] buffer
the_count_reader_0x66ed70.0x66ED8D: movzx eax, byte [eax+ecx]  -> RETURN ONE BYTE
the_count_reader_0x66ed70.0x66ED91: inc ecx ; [edx+0x1C] = ecx -> advance the BYTE cursor

what_this_proves: 0x66ED70 is NOT a bit reader: it returns a whole byte and advances a byte cursor at [+0x1C]
the bit reader used everywhere else (0x447190 / 0x66EC30) advances a different cursor
so the snapshot stream carries TWO cursors: one in bits, one in bytes
and the entity COUNT is taken from the BYTE stream, while the two gate bits before it come from the BIT stream
why_this_dissolves_a_lot_of_confusion: the project has been treating the snapshot as one continuous bit stream
if the count is byte-addressed, then inserting or removing bits anywhere before it changes which BYTE it reads
that explains why tiny changes at the ps block shifted the entity interpretation in ways that looked erratic
and it means the body must be built with BOTH a bit layout and a byte layout in mind
the_recipe_revised: bit 1 = 1 and bit 2 = 1 (from the bit stream)
then the next BYTE read by the byte cursor must be 0x01 (count = 1)
then 12 bits give the entity id
so the payload has to be arranged so that the byte cursor lands on a 0x01 byte at that moment
next: find where the byte cursor [+0x1C] is initialised for a snapshot, i.e. whether it starts at the same offset as the bit cursor or at a byte-aligned position
0x66ED70 reads [edx+0x1C] directly, so a probe on the stream struct before the entity block reveals both cursors at once
